evidence: "the canonical 64-query-head full-MHA geometry does not partition evenly into 3 ranks (64 heads / 64 KV heads into 3 ranks: 64/3 = 21.3, and the GQA variant's 8 KV heads — 64 query heads at an 8:1 ratio — do not divide into 3 ranks either, 8/3 = 2.67)"

evidence: "Only changing the attention mechanism itself (e.g., hybrid/linear attention) can reduce the growth rate: the layers it replaces hold a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing per-token cache, so a hybrid that still keeps some full-attention layers keeps growing — only more slowly — and only a model with no full-attention layers stops growing entirely (Ch 7, Fig 7.2) — KV offload changes where the cache resides, not how fast it grows."
issue: Dense run-on sentence (three em-dashes, three nested clauses) obscures the load-bearing distinction. It is difficult to parse whether 'only more slowly' refers to hybrid models or to the model with no full-attention layers.

A hybrid that keeps some full-attention layers grows more slowly; only a model with no full-attention layers stops growing entirely (Ch 7, Fig 7.2). fix_instruction: Either add the [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] labels to the first two rows and [canonical scenario][DERIVED] to the computed rows (matching Table 1-1's derivation column pattern), or change the header to '(assumed inputs and derived results of the canonical scenario)' rather than '(worked example, not reference)'.

chapter: Ch. 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference

chapter: Ch. 5 — From Workload to Model Selection
evidence: §5.3(a): "... ~186–371 ms if encoded on a single CPU core at ~30–60 GFLOP/s sustained (~200 GFLOP/s is the AVX-512 theoretical peak, not a sustained rate), but only ~1.1 ms on a ~10 TFLOP/s GPU, which is the basis the ~120 ms retrieval budget already assumes (vector search and reranking on a local GPU, Ch 4). On that basis the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget; single-core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core (11.14 GFLOP ÷ 0.12 s), beyond the typical sustained range (371 ms at 30 GFLOP/s vs 186 ms at 60 GFLOP/s) — conditional on measured single-core throughput."
issue: The sentence "the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget" is immediately contradicted by the figures in the same sentence for the CPU case (186–371 ms > 120 ms). The referent of "On that basis" is ambiguous: it can only mean the GPU figure (~1.1 ms), yet the following clause re-argues the CPU case, so the reader cannot tell which basis the claim is made on. The claim is also the hinge for the paragraph's conclusion that "the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget".
fix_instruction: Split the sentence and name the basis explicitly: "On a GPU (~1.1 ms at ~10 TFLOP/s) the incremental cost stays well within the ~120 ms retrieval budget; on a single CPU core it does not — 186–371 ms at 30–60 GFLOP/s — so single-core encoding fits only above ≈92.8 GFLOP/s sustained per core." Keep the numbers as they are; only the referents need to be disambiguated.
